turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell enquired whether Jack had any relatives in London and if not, what was to become of him during the winter months.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack explained to Lady Bracknell that he had no immediate relatives in London, but he assured her that he would take up residence in his club during the winter months.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell raised an eyebrow, enquiring if Mr Worthing was aware that gentlemen of independent means who lacked family ties were often considered somewhat suspect by those of the upper echelons of society.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack was somewhat taken aback by Lady Bracknell’s comment but assured her, in a polite and respectful manner, that he was well aware of the societal expectations and was committed to maintaining the highest standards of conduct and respectability.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell nodded curtly, her expression unyielding. She informed Jack that while his assurances were commendable, his lack of immediate family ties would indeed be a matter of concern for those in the upper echelons of society, and it would be prudent for him to consider acquiring a more substantial social network.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded respectfully, acknowledging Lady Bracknell’s concern and promising to consider her advice carefully.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell informed Jack, in a tone that left no room for argument, that while his intentions were commendable, he must also provide evidence of a stable and respectable lineage to be considered suitable for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack nodded, understanding the importance of his background, and assured Lady Bracknell that he would address this matter with diligence and sincerity.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell informed Jack, with a stern nod, that his assurances were appreciated but that he must also demonstrate a clear and unimpeachable lineage to be considered a suitable match for Gwendolen. The lady’s tone left no room for ambiguity.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the gravity of the situation, he told Lady Bracknell, and he would work diligently to address her concerns.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell was unimpressed by Jack’s assurances, informing him sternly that mere promises were insufficient. She demanded tangible evidence of a respectable lineage and social standing to proceed.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the weight of Lady Bracknell’s demands, he told her, and he would endeavor to provide the evidence needed to prove his respectability and suitability for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell was unimpressed by Jack’s earnestness, informing him with a condescending smile that mere efforts and promises were not enough. She demanded that he provide concrete proof of his respectability and impeccable social standing forthwith.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the gravity of the situation, he told Lady Bracknell, and he would work diligently to address her concerns.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell was unimpressed by Jack’s declarations, informing him with a stern nod that she required tangible proof of his social standing and impeccable lineage to even consider him a suitable match for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack understood the importance of Lady Bracknell’s demands, he told her, and would make every effort to provide the proof she required to demonstrate his respectability.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen was clearly frustrated with the proceedings, reproaching her mother, she told Lady Bracknell that she would not allow her engagement to Jack to be decided by such superficial criteria.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell was unmoved by Gwendolen’s protest, informing her daughter with a stern look that such matters were not to be trifled with and that she must adhere to the social standards that had been established.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen was dead tired of her mother's interference, she told Lady Bracknell, and she would not let her dictate who she could or could not marry.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell was unyielding, telling Gwendolen that such matters were none of her concern and that she would not be dictated to by her whims.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
